verses.text: We know that if our earthly tent—this body we live in—is destroyed, God has a building ready for us: an eternal home in heaven, not made by human hands.
While we're in this tent, we groan and long to put on our heavenly home,
if indeed, when we put it on, we won't be found naked.
While we're in this tent, we groan under the burden. We don't want to be unclothed; we want to be clothed with our heavenly home, so that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.
God is the one who prepared us for this very thing, and he gave us the Spirit as a guarantee.
So we're always confident. We know that as long as we live in the body, we're away from the Lord,
because we live by faith, not by what we see.
We're confident, I say, and would rather leave the body and be at home with the Lord.
So whether we're at home in the body or away from it, our goal is to please him.
We must all appear before Christ's judgment seat, so each person may receive what is due for what they did in the body, whether good or bad.
Because we know what it means to fear the Lord, we try to persuade people. God already knows us completely, and I hope you know us in your conscience too.
We're not trying to recommend ourselves to you again. We're giving you a reason to be proud of us, so you'll have an answer for those who boast about appearances instead of the heart.
If we seem out of our minds, it's for God; if we're clear-minded, it's for you.
Christ's love compels us, because we've concluded this: one died for everyone, and so everyone died.
He died for everyone so that those who live would no longer live for themselves, but for the one who died and was raised for them.
So from now on, we don't judge anyone from a merely human point of view. Even if we once viewed Christ that way, we don't anymore.
So if anyone is in Christ, they are a new creation. The old has passed away; look, the new has come!
All this comes from God, who reconciled us to himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation:
God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, no longer counting people's trespasses against them. And he entrusted us with the message of reconciliation.
So we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God were making his appeal through us. We beg you on Christ's behalf: be reconciled to God.
God made the one who knew no sin to be a sin offering for us, so that in him we could become God's righteousness.
